comment: No building elevation sheets provided showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimension annotations. Site plan is 2D top-down view only; no vertical elevation views are available.
applicableAreas: all buildings (buildings 1-8)

comment: No section or profile view exhibits provided showing dimension lines from outer conductor to building edges. Horizontal clearance dimensions shown on site plan (26.1', 29.6', 21.3') but no vertical sections or enlarged details demonstrating clearances from conductor to building projections.
applicableAreas: all buildings and projections (buildings 1-8)

comment: No cross-section or profile views provided showing vertical clearance from finished driveway grades to lowest point of overhead electric facilities. Grading plan provides top-down view with spot elevations but no section views with conductor heights shown.
applicableAreas: driveways throughout site

comment: No vertical clearance sections or profile views provided showing finished driveway/road grades relative to overhead transmission line heights. Requirement: 30-foot minimum vertical clearance from road surface to electric transmission line. No dimension annotations or cross-sections demonstrating compliance exist.
applicableAreas: driveways and site grading near transmission lines

comment: Clearance dimensions are shown on site plan (26.1', 29.6', 21.3'), but measurement origin (from outside conductor vs. from pole centerline) cannot be verified from available documentation. UCM § 1.10.3 requires measurement from outside conductor, not pole centerline.
applicableAreas: western and eastern site boundaries

comment: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey provided showing pole locations and vertical clearances from overhead transmission facilities to site features. When vertical clearance from overhead facilities to proposed site features appears marginal or insufficient based on site plan data, surveyor verification is required.
applicableAreas: buildings and driveways with overhead transmission lines

comment: Three mitigation trees are shown on landscape plan within 10-15 feet of overhead electric line (southern boundary), but specific tree species are not identified. Requirement: trees within 50 lateral feet of overhead transmission conductors must be utility-compatible species (generally mature height ≤20 feet per ECM Appendix F). Species verification cannot be completed.
applicableAreas: landscape areas adjacent to overhead transmission line on southern/eastern boundary

comment: No construction logistics plan, equipment operation zone map, or work platform plan provided showing 10-foot radial clearance from overhead transmission lines. OSHA and Texas law require 20-foot clearance during construction near energized transmission lines (per Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes item #3). Construction staging clearance verification is not documented.
applicableAreas: entire construction site with overhead transmission lines

comment: Trees marked as 'M' (Mitigation) and 'P' (Parking Buffer) are positioned 5-10 feet from the overhead electric (OHE) line on the landscape plan, which falls within the < 15 lateral feet distribution restriction zone requiring utility-compatible species only. However, the landscape plan does not identify which specific species are labeled with these symbols, and the plant list on Sheet 35 does not indicate which of the four proposed shade/ornamental species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) are the 'M' and 'P' trees. Without species identification linked to tree symbol locations, and without ECM Appendix F utility-compatible designations, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary area within 15 lateral feet of OHE line

comment: Trees are positioned within 25 feet of the overhead electric line. The requirement prohibits large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) within this zone. However, the landscape plan does not differentiate which trees are 'large trees' (40+ feet mature height). Sheet 35 lists species with their container size specifications but does not document mature heights per ECM Appendix F. Without mature height documentation linked to tree locations on the plan, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary area within 25 lateral feet of OHE line

comment: Overhead electric poles are shown on the landscape plan as circular symbols with 'x' marks along the OHE line on the southern boundary. Trees marked 'M' and 'P' are positioned 5-10 feet from the OHE line. The requirement prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of utility poles. However, the landscape plan does not provide exact dimensions from tree trunk centers to pole centerlines, and the 'M' and 'P' tree species are not identified on the plan. Without exact measurements and species identification, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary area along Valley View Road

comment: Trees proposed near the overhead electric line on the landscape plan are labeled with functional designations ('M' for Mitigation, 'P' for Parking Buffer) but the landscape plan does not directly identify the botanical or common names of these specific trees. The plant list on Sheet 35 specifies species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) but does not cross-reference which species are labeled 'M' or 'P' on the actual drawing. A reviewer must reference multiple sheets and cannot directly correlate tree symbols on the landscape plan to specific species. Provide a clear plant legend on the landscape plan that identifies the species of each labeled tree, or clearly reference the plant schedule with species names linked to drawing symbols.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan near overhead electric facilities (southern boundary area)

comment: The landscape plan does not differentiate or designate large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) from smaller trees. Tree symbols on the plan are marked by functional category ('M', 'P', 'SY', 'PL') but include no notation, color-coding, or legend entry identifying which trees are 'large' (≥40 feet mature height). The plant schedule on Sheet 35 does not document mature heights per ECM Appendix F. Large trees positioned within 25 feet of overhead distribution facilities require specific clearance compliance; without identification of large trees on the plan, such compliance cannot be verified. Provide a clear designation (notation, color, legend symbol) on the landscape plan identifying trees with mature heights of 40 feet or greater per ECM Appendix F.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan near overhead electric facilities (southern boundary area)

comment: The landscape plan does not provide dimension lines or measurements from tree trunk centers to the overhead electric line or from the OHE line to utility poles. While pole symbols are shown on the OHE line, no dimensions or calculations are provided to demonstrate that clearances are measured from the outside conductor (not pole centerline). Without dimensional evidence on the plan, the measurement methodology cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary area along Valley View Road

comment: The landscape plan does not provide dimension lines or measurements from tree locations. Without dimensioned evidence showing whether measurements originate at tree trunk centers (planting locations) or at projected canopy edges, the measurement methodology cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary area along Valley View Road

comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows the overhead electric (OHE) line and poles along the southern boundary. However, the electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows only underground electrical infrastructure; the two plans do not clearly cross-reference or align. While the OHE line is present on the landscape plan, a reviewer must cross-reference between sheets to verify that all overhead conductors and poles are depicted on the landscape plan. The electrical plan should be referenced or overlaid on the landscape plan to provide complete clarity on overhead facility locations and ensure all conductors are shown relative to tree locations.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan (entire site)

comment: Trees are positioned within restricted clearance zones (5-10 feet from the OHE line and utility poles along the southern boundary). The plans do not provide evidence of Austin Energy written approval for these placements. No approval letters, correspondence, or notes in the submitted site plan documents indicate that Austin Energy has authorized the tree placement in these restricted zones. If trees within prohibited zones are proposed, documented written approval from Austin Energy must be provided on or attached to the site plan.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary area within 15 lateral feet of OHE line and near utility poles

comment: Vision analysis estimates clearances of 5-10 feet and 10-15 feet from buildings; however, no explicit dimension callouts are provided on the electrical plan to verify that minimum 5-foot clearances are maintained.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations

comment: Transformer pad locations are shown on the electrical plan, but building elevation sheets do not contain callouts or dimensions showing balcony or overhang locations relative to the transformer pads, preventing verification of 5-foot lateral clearances.
applicableAreas: Building elevation zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: The transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on the electrical plan; building elevations are not coordinated with transformer locations to verify 12-foot clearances from windows, doors, or ventilating ducts.
applicableAreas: Building window/door zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Sidewalk easements are labeled on the electrical plan, but specific sidewalk locations and distances from transformer pads are not dimensioned on the plan.
applicableAreas: Sidewalk zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified; fire escape locations are not shown on the electrical plan relative to transformer pads, preventing verification of 20-foot clearances.
applicableAreas: Fire escape zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Transformer pad access door orientation and location are not identified on the electrical plan. Without knowing which side of each pad is the access door side, the 10-foot hot-stick clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations

comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows tree and vegetation symbols but does not explicitly identify which trees are within 10 lateral feet of specific transformer pad locations or 15 lateral feet of overhead conductors. Plant list (Sheets 32, 35) identifies species but does not correlate species with proximity zones or provide utility-compatible classifications per ECM Appendix F.
applicableAreas: Tree/vegetation zones within 10-15 lateral feet of transformer pads and overhead distribution lines

comment: Landscape plan shows shrub and groundcover planting symbols and plant schedule specifies shrub types (Dwarf Palmetto, Big Muhly, Gulf Muhly, Texas Sage, Dwarf Wax Myrtle) but does not correlate specific shrub locations to transformer pad access door orientations or verify 10-foot and 5-foot lateral clearances.
applicableAreas: Shrub/vegetation zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Landscape plan shows tree locations and plant schedule identifies tree species, but transformer pad locations are not marked on the landscape plan, and no root barrier details are shown in the construction detail sheets for trees in proximity to transformer pads.
applicableAreas: Tree zones within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment

comment: The Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) may designate fire lanes, but the electrical plan (Sheet 21) does not show fire lane locations relative to transformer pads with dimension callouts demonstrating 15-foot clearances.
applicableAreas: Fire lane zones near transformer pads

comment: Water supply lines are labeled on the electrical plan with 'W' callouts near transformer pads, but no dimension callouts specify the clearance distance from transformer pads to water lines. Clearance compliance cannot be verified without explicit dimensions.
applicableAreas: Water utility zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Wastewater lines are labeled on the electrical plan with 'WW' callouts near transformer pads, but no dimension callouts specify the clearance distance from transformer pads to wastewater lines. Clearance compliance cannot be verified without explicit dimensions.
applicableAreas: Wastewater utility zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Storm drain infrastructure is shown on the Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) and general utilities are referenced on the electrical plan (Sheet 21), but no explicit dimension callouts show clearance distances from transformer pads to storm drain lines.
applicableAreas: Storm drain utility zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Gas infrastructure is not clearly shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) relative to transformer pad locations. The plan does not specify whether gas service is present on the site or what clearance distances are maintained.

comment: Underground utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain, electric, telecommunications) are identified on the electrical plan, but no explicit horizontal or vertical clearance dimensions are provided showing 12-inch minimum separations between transformer pads and these utilities.
applicableAreas: Underground utility zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: The electrical plan shows multiple utility lines and transformer pads, but does not explicitly analyze or document whether transformer pads or AE underground facilities are located directly over or under other utility lines, or whether customer buildings/parking are located over AE facilities.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads and underground facilities relative to other utilities and structures

comment: Overhead electric distribution lines (OHE) are shown on the electrical plan near several transformer pad locations (particularly on western and southern property edges), but no explicit dimension callouts show the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance distances.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric line zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: Overhead distribution lines are shown on the plan but are not analyzed with 15-foot radius clearance circles or dimension callouts. No explicit documentation confirms that transformer locations and proposed facilities maintain the 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution conductor zones adjacent to transformer pads

comment: No cross-section drawings are provided on any plan sheet showing vertical clearances from ground to overhead structures (building overhangs, canopies, garage structures) at transformer pad locations. While overhead structures may exist (buildings, parking structures), vertical clearance documentation is absent.
applicableAreas: Vertical clearance zones with overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas

comment: The Grading Plan (Sheet 11) does not depict transformer pad locations, making it impossible to verify whether surface drainage slopes are directed away from buildings as required for oil-filled equipment. Additionally, the electrical plan does not specify whether transformers are oil-filled or dry-type.
applicableAreas: Grading/drainage zones around transformer pad locations

comment: Vision analysis indicates that two of the five transformer pads (located west of Buildings 2 and 8) are positioned OUTSIDE the main property boundary, within a 'Sidewalk Easement' area between the private property line and the public right-of-way. All pad-mounted transformer equipment must be located 100% on private property, not in public right-of-way or easements.
applicableAreas: Two transformer pads located on western property edge (west of Buildings 2 and 8)

comment: Two transformer pads appear to be located within a 'Sidewalk Easement' area. Additionally, the facts.md document identifies a perpetual City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 acres, NE corner, Instrument 2011021137) that is not depicted on the submitted site plan. Transformer pads cannot be placed in drainage easements, sewer easements, water easements, or electrical easements under overhead lines without explicit Austin Energy Design written approval.
applicableAreas: Two transformer pads within sidewalk easement (west of Buildings 2 and 8); all five transformer pads relative to drainage easement

comment: Dashed rectangular boundaries are shown around the five transformer pad locations, with one labeled 'Vault Easement' (near Bldg 8). However, no easement widths or dimensions are specified for any of the five locations. Austin Energy Design accessibility requirements determine the required easement width, but this width is not documented on the plans.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations

comment: Electrical routing lines are shown from transformer pads to meters on Sheet 21, but the routing paths are not explicitly verified to remain 100% on private property. Given that two transformer pads are located in the 'Sidewalk Easement' (outside private property), the electrical conduit routing from those pads would also be outside private property, violating the requirement that electrical routing be 100% on private property.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters, particularly for the two pads located in sidewalk easement

comment: Transformer pad dimensions are not labeled on any plan sheet (estimated 8'x8' to 10'x10' by visual scale only). No references to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail specifications are provided. The electrical specifications do not identify the service type (single-phase vs. three-phase). Without this documentation, transformer pad construction dimensions cannot be verified to match AE Design-approved specifications for the specified service type.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations

comment: Vision analysis confirms that all five transformer pads are located immediately adjacent to or within 4 feet of driveways, parking aisles, or vehicle circulation routes. However, NO bollards or protective posts are shown on the electrical plan. The plan lacks any callouts, notations, or specifications for 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards required by AE Design equipment pad details when pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations
